title: Nine Words I Got Wrong
subtitle: 语言文化 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 语言文化（历史社会与文化·语言与文化）
meta: 主题语境：语言文化（历史社会与文化·语言与文化）　|　核心词汇：word　|　正文 409 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 word 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: I learned English from a teacher who never praised anybody, and the only ① word of approval I ever got from him was 'adequate', written in the margin of an essay about rain. I looked it up. It was not the ② word I hoped for and it was, I now think, exactly the word I needed: precise, unflattering, and true.

He never wasted a ③ word and he never repeated one, which made the back of the room a dangerous place to sit. He had one rule about dictionaries: a word is not its definition, a word is the company it keeps. He made us copy sentences rather than lists, and for two years I thought this was laziness. It was the opposite: he was teaching us that no ④ word travels alone, and that a vocabulary learned in columns is a vocabulary you cannot use.

In that room his ⑤ word was law, and nobody tested it twice. He gave his ⑥ word that we would never be tested on lists, and in eleven terms he never was. The word he most disliked was 'nice' — not because it is vague, though it is, but because it ends conversations: once something is nice, there is nothing left to ask. 'Give me the ⑦ word for the thing,' he would say, 'not the word for your opinion of it.' I have ⑧ worded letters since then with that sentence in my head, and it has never once made a letter worse.

In the fourth year he gave us a test with no instructions, only a line at the top: 'Write what you think this means.' Half the class wrote nothing. I wrote four paragraphs and got a C, with 'adequate' again in the margin. He told me afterwards that a word has two jobs — to say and to signal — and that I had spent four paragraphs signalling. It was the most useful thing anybody said to me that year.

⑨ Word came on a Tuesday, in an email from the school, four years after I last saw him. I never wrote the letter I meant to write, and I have regretted the ⑩ wording of that omission ever since, which is a very English way to feel. What I have instead is a habit: when a word will not come, I do not reach for a better one. I wait, and the sentence tells me what it needs, and that, I think, was the whole lesson.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 话语；所说的话（waste a word）
C. n. 消息；音信（word came that ...）
D. n. 诺言；保证（give one's word）
E. v. 措辞；写（word a letter）
F. n. 措辞；说法（the wording of）
G. n. 命令；指示；权威的话
H. n. 评语；评价（a word of approval）

items.q: It was not the word I hoped for
He gave his word that we would never be tested on lists
Give me the word for the thing
I have worded letters since then

answers.why: a word of approval 意为“一句赞许的话、评语”，此处指 adequate 这个评语。
指“我”盼望的那个“词”，说它不是我以为的那个词，却正是需要的词。
waste a word 意为“浪费话语”，指他从不说废话、从不重复。
同样是“词”，说没有哪个词是单独行走的，故要抄句子而非词表。
one's word is law 意为“某人的话就是命令”，说他在教室里一言九鼎。
give one's word 意为“作出保证、许诺”，说他保证过永不考单词表，且十一个学期都做到了。
指“指称某物的词”，与“表达你评价的词”相对。
word 作动词，意为“措辞、写”，说此后写信都记着那句话。
Word came ... 意为“消息传来”，指四年后校方发来的那封邮件。
wording 意为“措辞、说法”，此处带自嘲：连这份疏漏的说法我都在意。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 我从他那里得到的唯一一句赞许是 adequate。（a word of approval）
他从不浪费话语，也从不重复一句。（waste a word）
在那间教室里，他的话就是命令。（one's word is law）
他保证过永不考单词表，而且做到了。（give one's word）
给我指称事物的词，而不是表达你评价的词。（the word for）
消息是在一个周二传来的，来自学校的一封邮件。（word came）
answers: The only word of approval I ever got from him was 'adequate'.
He never wasted a word and he never repeated one.
In that room his word was law.
He gave his word that we would never be tested on lists, and he never was.
Give me the word for the thing, not the word for your opinion of it.
Word came on a Tuesday, in an email from the school.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 word 的 3 种不同用法；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: A word, my teacher said, is not its definition; a word is the company it keeps.
He never wasted a word, and he never repeated one.
In that room his word was law, and he gave his word that we would never be tested on lists.
'Give me the word for the thing,' he would say, 'not the word for your opinion of it.'
I have worded letters ever since with that sentence in my head.
Word came on a Tuesday, and I have regretted the wording of my silence ever since.
